chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: How they got out of Boston: the maid's $300
summary: A friend working as an actress's maid lent about $300 for the trip to New York without costumes or music.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, what did you do back in Boston when you were left with no money. How did you leave, where did you get the money from?

I got it through a friend of mine working in a theater not so far from where we were as a maid to one of the actresses called -- oh, I can't think of her name. But however, she was a maid for one of the acrosses around the corner from the theater we were and she let me have the money, about $300 for Buck and I to go to New York. So we went to New York without the costumes and music that we needed to go and do our act, 'cause we had nothing, they kept our clothes, you know and the trunk and all in the theater in Boston. So we had to get some more material and all to work with. So we did. That's when we got the job with John T. Gibson in Philadelphia.
